sources.name: Marie_Haynes
sources.excerpt: Google announced that AI Overviews and AI Mode are going to do more when it comes to linking out to websites. 1. More inline links in AI answers. Plus they will be shown higher up in responses more frequently. 2. Displaying official websites up high in AI answers if they are the place where people usually go to complete a specific tasks. 3. New prominent carousels for timely news articles that will appear within the AI answers. These will highlight your Preferred Sources. 4. More links to websites at the end of AI answers, along with image thumbnails and a more clickable design. 5. Clickable creator and publisher names on video results that take you to their Search Profile.…

AI Search / GEO.what_happened: Rank tracking is broken right now. “Poisoned SERPs” have hit almost every data provider. But there’s still a way to…

sources.name: brodieseo
sources.excerpt: Rank tracking is broken right now. “Poisoned SERPs” have hit almost every data provider. But there’s still a way to build accurate and detailed ranking reports for clients, using a method Google hasn’t blocked (yet). The setup: 1. Connect the @serplens MCP to Claude Desktop 2. Create a destination for the data (I use Notion) 3. Ask Claude to run scheduled ranking checks It works because the SERP Lens browser strips /goto links by default, and Claude can switch the VPN location through the MCP. I’ve got it checking a client’s keywords from Sydney every morning, logging rank, URL and SERP features automatically. Comment “SERP” and I’ll send you the full setup guide. h/t @suganthan for…
sources.author: @brodieseo

AI Search / GEO.what_happened: Google doesn’t label AI Mode queries in Search Console, but they leave a trace: people reply to an AI, and the reply…

sources.name: aleyda
sources.excerpt: Google doesn’t label AI Mode queries in Search Console, but they leave a trace: people reply to an AI, and the reply gets logged as a search: @jwbobbink classified every query of 155 sites over 16 months to see how often that happens, and how fast it’s growing 👇 Here are key insights: * Replies typed at an AI are now normal. Bare replies such as “yes”, “ja” or “yes please” showed up as searches on 94 of the 155 sites. Per million impressions they grew from 5.6 to 116: 21 times as many in 16 months. * German speakers say please to an AI, Indonesian speakers don’t. Three in four German yes-replies come with “bitte” or “gerne” (“ja bitte” on 52 sites). Dutch speakers add “graag” two times in…
